\begin{document}
A no-break space before inline math, as in the value of~$x$, keeps the
math on the line of the word before it. So does a thin space, as in
p.\,$5$. A no-break space or a thin space after inline math keeps the
word after it on the same line, as in $x$~and, $5$\,cm, and
$x$~$y$.

Lemma~$1$ cites pp.\,$3$--$4$, where the set of~$n$~elements is
$y$~times the size of~$z$, and $A$\,m\textsuperscript{2} is an area.
\end{document}
